newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels Bel-20 within reach of 2,000-level.
newsitem.headline: Brussels Bel-20 within reach of 2,000-level.

text.p: Belgian shares pushed into unchartered territory on Monday, setting an all-time record high close as investors flocked to the market confident that the bourse could rise further in coming weeks.

"There is no reason for the market to come back down, the dollar is strong, rates are good, fundamentals are good and there's a lot of derivative products on the Belgian market," said trader Paul de Lophem at brokerage Mignon, Hanart, Declerck.
The blue-chip Bel-20 index closed up 1.57 percent, or 30.57 points, at 1,975.56.
"Maybe the sky's the limit but we'll certainly reach 2,000 by the end of the week," de Lophem said.
Trader Benoit Kint at Petercam said guaranteed index funds had helped push the bourse higher.
Dealers said industrial stocks remained the main attraction on the Bel-20 index with chemicals firm Solvay climbing an impressive 5.58 percent to close at 21,750 francs.
"Chemical prices are up, the dollar effect and the acquisition (60 percent stake in Bulgarian soda producer SODI) led to the fantastic rise we've seen," said analyst Jurgen Fryges at KB-Securities.
Dealers said pharmaceutical products Solvay was developing had further tempted investors to pick up the stock.
De Lophem said Solvay's anti-depression drug Flesinoxan could compete with the blockbuster drug Prozac in the U.S.
Chemicals and drugs group UCB gained 1.65 percent to close at 86,400 francs.
"We think UCB will remain strong because of its blockbuster product Zyrtec," said another trader.
He added that UCB could reach 100,000 francs once it made an annoucement on when it would receive approval to sell Zyrtec in Japan, the second largest pharmaceutical market in the world.
Retailer Delhaize pushed higher on the back of a strong dollar and investors' confidence in the cyclical stock.
It closed up 2.27 percent to 2,030 francs with a high volume of 184,462 shares traded.
Oil and chemicals firm Petrofina was up 2.05 percent at 11,225 francs, lifted by the strong dollar.
Brokerage Vermeulen-Raemdonck said in its weekly market report on Friday that it rated Petrofina a buy (11,000 BEF).
Fina Inc a unit of Petrofina announced it had acquired a minority stake in a joint-venture in convenience stores in the U.S.
